prompt: Why subtract each user’s row mean before cosine similarity in the user-based method?
explanation: Centering removes each user’s rating baseline so cosine similarity compares deviations and preference pattern.
misconception: Using raw rating magnitudes; user-based cosine compares deviations from each user's mean.
visualHook: Subtract row means and circle only the co-rated centered entries.
choices: To compare deviations rather than generosity
To create more movies
To make every rating positive
To replace the latent-factor model

prompt: If $q=(2,-1)$ and $p=(3,4)$, what does the latent-factor dot-product predictor return?
choices: $q\cdot p=2\cdot3+(-1)\cdot4=2$
$q\cdot p=2\cdot3+1\cdot4=10$
explanation: Multiply matching coordinates and add: $2\cdot3+(-1)\cdot4=6-4=2$. Norm products, coordinate sums, and division are different operations.
misconception: Changing the dot product into a norm or forgetting the negative-coordinate product.
visualHook: Write the first coordinate product and the signed second coordinate product separately, then add them.

prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two recommender methods used in Assignment 2?
choices: User-based filtering uses centered ratings from similar users; latent factors learn vectors and use $q_u\cdot p_i$
Both methods use the same centered-neighbour average; only the notation changes
User-based filtering learns one vector per item, while latent factors compare raw user rows
Latent factors require an exact overlap between users, while user-based filtering does not
User-based filtering predicts with $q_u\cdot p_i$, while latent factors use only row means
The methods are conceptually identical whenever they predict the same missing matrix entry
explanation: User-based filtering derives a prediction from similar users and their centered observed ratings. Latent factors learn low-dimensional user and item vectors whose dot product estimates a rating; sharing an output does not make the models identical.
misconception: Blending neighborhood and latent-factor formulas into one predictor.
visualHook: Draw two lanes: centered neighbors on one side and q·p on the other.

prompt: A new user has no known ratings. Which part of the user-based workflow fails first?
choices: The user's row mean and centered-overlap similarities are undefined without a fallback
The item vectors $p_i$ disappear, so every latent-factor prediction is undefined
Cosine similarity becomes $1$ because an empty profile matches every user
The target item must be removed because no user can rate it
The global mean becomes undefined because one user has no ratings
The neighbourhood is known exactly from the item popularity alone
explanation: The user-based workflow needs a profile to compute a row mean and similarities on overlapping rated items. A prior, onboarding signal, or popularity fallback is required; an empty row is not evidence of maximum similarity.
misconception: Treating missing ratings as zeros; cold start has no overlap or user mean to use.
visualHook: Show the empty rating row and mark the missing prerequisites for similarity.
